state.product: MenteViva, iOS cognitive-exercise app: 5 warm-toned games (memory pairs, Stroop, category fluency, adaptive math, visual discrimination), offline-first, EN/ES bilingual, no accounts, no clinical scores. Zero third-party deps, solo developer. Copy ceiling: 'fun mental exercise' — no medical claims ever (FDA general-wellness line; FTC fined Lumosity $2M; App Store 1.4.1).
state.product_truth: Primary player is an older family member who needs errorless, familiar play. Jev request 008 ruled allocate-not-delete: familiarity-based games serve that player, other games serve mom/owner. Per-person libraries are the north star. Informal playtest: scoring confusing, games get boring, not visually attractive.

market_evidence.S1_older_adults_60plus: 1.1B people 60+ worldwide (2023) doubling to 2.1B by 2050 (WHO). 52.7M Americans 50+ play video games = 45% of that population (AARP 2023). Incumbents (Lumosity 100M registered, Elevate 50M downloads) are generic, subscription-priced, not dementia-adapted. Our edge: errorless low-failure design, one-time price, EN+ES.
market_evidence.CH_caregiver_channel: 63M US family caregivers (AARP/NAC 2025). Adult child installs and pays; parent plays. Attach rate unknown.
market_evidence.S2_mental_health: ~15% of adults 70+ live with a mental disorder (WHO 2026). Mental-health apps market vendor-estimated $17.5B by 2030. Serving them as patients = medical device = FDA; serving them as adjacent wellness users adds no design freedom beyond S1 overlap.
market_evidence.S3_general_wellness: Mature crowded category (Calm/Headspace/Lumosity). No differentiation beyond one-time price and bilingual. No primary demand stat found.

state.constraints: Design/copy focus decision only — no code forks, one binary. Warm-failure tone. Zero deps. Engagement of the primary segment is still unproven (G1b gate).

primary_segment.instructions: Which segment should MenteViva's DESIGN and COPY primarily optimize for, given one binary and no code forks?

criteria.older_adults_60plus: Older adults 60+ including early cognitive decline; largest growing demographic, proven 50+ gaming demand, our differentiated edge (errorless design, one-time price, bilingual)
criteria.mental_health_adjacent: Adults managing mental health; large but overlapping with older adults, adds regulatory gravity, zero incremental design freedom
criteria.general_wellness: General wellness adults; mature category where we have no edge beyond price and language

sell_to_caregiver.instructions: Should marketing and purchase flow primarily address the adult-child caregiver (the buyer) rather than the player themselves?

criteria.true: The 63M-caregiver channel is the realistic purchase path for the primary segment and the buyer already co-uses the app
criteria.false: Players mostly discover and buy the app themselves; caregiver-first marketing would miss them

copy_ceiling_holds.instructions: Given expansion to mental-health and wellness segments, should the non-clinical copy ceiling ('fun mental exercise', no claims) remain unchanged?

criteria.true: Wider audiences raise, not lower, the value of staying clearly on the general-wellness side of FDA/FTC/App Store lines
criteria.false: Serving mental-health users well requires softening the no-claims ceiling
